dataLineageViz.maxNodes.markdownDescription: Maximum number of database objects admitted to the webview working graph. The complete host snapshot remains available to `@lineage`; virtual external nodes are added only while this budget permits. React Flow rendering is separately capped by `renderLimit`.

dataLineageViz.renderLimit.markdownDescription: Maximum rendered nodes before showing a warning instead of the graph. Prevents browser performance issues with very large visualizations. AI tools and BFS operate on the full model regardless of this limit.

dataLineageViz.excludePatterns.markdownDescription: Regex patterns applied when a source is opened to exclude objects from the webview graph (e.g. `_TEST$`, `^staging\\.`). Matched against `schema.object`; `%` is accepted as a wildcard. Requires reloading the data source to take effect. The complete host snapshot remains available to `@lineage`. For ad-hoc filtering without reload, use the Exclusion Rules toolbar button.

dataLineageViz.externalRefs.enabled.markdownDescription: Detect external references (OPENROWSET file paths, cross-database 3-part names). When disabled, no virtual external nodes are created. External Tables are unaffected. Requires reloading the data source to take effect.

dataLineageViz.overview.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable Schema View. When enabled and a loaded graph exceeds `overview.threshold` nodes, the graph starts in schema-level cluster nodes; at or below the threshold it starts in Object View. After load, the toolbar Object View / Schema View toggle controls the surface until Reset All or a new load.

dataLineageViz.overview.threshold.markdownDescription: Controls whether the graph defaults to Schema View or the classic Object View on initial load. If the loaded database has more nodes than this threshold, it starts in Schema View. At or below this threshold, it starts fully expanded in the classic Object View (meaning users with smaller databases will not notice any difference on startup). This is evaluated only on initial load or 'Reset All'.

enumDescriptions: Double-clicking a schema adds it to Expanded Schema View.
Double-clicking a schema makes it the only expanded schema.
dataLineageViz.overview.schemaDoubleClic.markdownDescription: Controls what double-clicking a schema node does in Schema View. `expand` adds the schema to Expanded Schema View; `expandOnly` makes the clicked schema the only expanded schema.

dataLineageViz.parseRulesFile.markdownDescription: Path to a custom parse rules YAML file. Leave empty for built-in defaults. [Customization guide](https://github.com/ChrisDevRepo/vscode_data_lineage/blob/main/docs/PARSE_RULES.md)

dataLineageViz.dmvQueryTimeout.markdownDescription: Timeout (seconds) per DMV query. Increase for large databases.

dataLineageViz.dmvQueriesFile.markdownDescription: Path to a custom DMV queries YAML file. Leave empty for built-in defaults. [Customization guide](https://github.com/ChrisDevRepo/vscode_data_lineage/blob/main/docs/DMV_QUERIES.md)

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.enabled.markdownDescription: Show column statistics and row counts in the table design viewer (database import only).

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.standardM.markdownDescription: Allow **Standard** profiling mode (adds AVG, STDEV, zero/empty counts). When `false`, only Quick mode is available — lighter queries.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.excludeEx.markdownDescription: Skip profiling for external tables. External tables query remote data sources (S3, Blob, other databases) — profiling can be slow and expensive.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.sampleThr.markdownDescription: Advanced: Tables above this row count use sampling instead of a full scan. Set to `0` to always sample.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.sampleSiz.markdownDescription: Advanced: Number of rows to sample when profiling large tables.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.useApprox.markdownDescription: Advanced: Use `APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT` instead of exact `COUNT(DISTINCT)`. Much faster with ~2% margin. Requires SQL Server 2019+.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.maxColumn.markdownDescription: Advanced: Maximum number of columns to profile per table. Columns beyond this cap are skipped. Prevents massive queries on wide tables.

dataLineageViz.layout.direction.markdownDescription: Direction of the dependency graph layout.

enumDescriptions: Smooth step edges with rounded corners

dataLineageViz.layout.edgeAnimation.markdownDescription: Animate edges when running a trace.

dataLineageViz.layout.highlightAnimation.markdownDescription: Animate edges when clicking a node.

dataLineageViz.layout.minimapEnabled.markdownDescription: Show the graph minimap for navigation.

dataLineageViz.layout.rankSeparation.markdownDescription: Advanced: Horizontal spacing between dependency layers (pixels).

dataLineageViz.layout.nodeSeparation.markdownDescription: Advanced: Vertical spacing between nodes in the same layer (pixels).

dataLineageViz.trace.defaultUpstreamLeve.markdownDescription: How many levels upstream (inputs) to trace by default.

dataLineageViz.trace.defaultDownstreamLe.markdownDescription: How many levels downstream (outputs) to trace by default.

dataLineageViz.analysis.hubMinDegree.markdownDescription: Minimum number of connections for an object to appear in the hub list.

dataLineageViz.analysis.islandMaxSize.markdownDescription: Max connected component size to qualify as an island. Higher values include larger disconnected subgraphs; set lower (e.g. 5) to focus on small isolated pairs/groups only.

dataLineageViz.analysis.longestPathMinNo.markdownDescription: Minimum number of objects in a dependency chain for longest-path analysis.

dataLineageViz.ai.enabled.description: Enable the @lineage chat participant and AI lineage tools. Disable for users who do not use VS Code Copilot or want to remove AI features entirely.

dataLineageViz.ai.maxRounds.markdownDescription: Maximum tool-call rounds per `@lineage` request. Increase for complex explorations on deep graphs. Each round is one AI reasoning step + tool call. Requires reloading the window to take effect.

dataLineageViz.ai.discoveryNodeCap.markdownDescription: Maximum scope nodes the AI may pull during a single discovery-phase catalog request before the engine forces an SM escalation via the gate. Discovery answers small ad-hoc questions in chat; over-budget requests are rejected with a hint to call `lineage_start_exploration`.

dataLineageViz.ai.discoveryTokenBudget.markdownDescription: Maximum estimated DDL tokens for a single discovery-phase catalog request. Exceeding either this or the node cap forces an SM escalation via the consent gate.

dataLineageViz.ai.explorationNodeCap.markdownDescription: Maximum total scope nodes during consent-approved active exploration. Each hop's accepted routes are admission-checked before scope grows; an over-budget submission is held and rejected with a hint to prune, defer, or synthesize.

dataLineageViz.ai.explorationTokenBudget.markdownDescription: Maximum estimated cumulative DDL tokens for the active exploration scope. The effective budget is additionally capped to a share of the selected model's input window, so smaller bring-your-own-key models shrink it automatically.

dataLineageViz.ai.outputTemplateFile.markdownDescription: Path to custom AI output templates YAML. Controls how `@lineage` formats summary, description, badges, highlights, and notes. Leave empty for built-in defaults. Use Command Palette → *Create AI Output Templates* to scaffold. [Customization guide](https://github.com/ChrisDevRepo/vscode_data_lineage/blob/main/docs/AI_PROMPTS.md)

languageModelTools.name: lineage_get_context
languageModelTools.userDescription: Shows what is currently loaded and visible in the lineage graph.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the current database context including loaded schemas, stats, and active UI filters.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_search_objects
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search for database objects by name or column.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search database objects by name or column name using substring or regex matching. Returns object IDs and metadata. Each result carries an `in_user_filter` flag — when an in-filter search returns 0 hits but out-of-filter results exist, include that schema in the next search; the active filter is a display preference, not a boundary.

query.description: Object name or column name to search for. At least 2 characters, never '*' — e.g. "SalesOrder". May be empty ONLY together with schemas[] to list everything in those schemas. Do not include schema prefixes like '[dbo].'.

schemas.description: Optional schema-name filter; use with an empty query to list objects in those schemas.

mode.description: Name matching strategy; substring is the normal discovery default.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_get_object_detail
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get full details for a specific database object.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Primary single-object lookup for discovery and synthesis. Use this when the user asks about one specific object (DDL, columns, direct neighbors). For graph-scope lineage questions, prefer lineage_get_scope_bundle instead of chaining repeated per-node detail calls.

id.description: Canonical object ID returned by a lineage search or scope tool.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_detect_graph_patterns
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find structural patterns like hubs, cycles, or orphans in the graph.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Analyzes the entire graph for specific structural patterns such as hubs, islands, orphans, longest paths, cycles, or external references.

min_degree.description: Minimum node degree for hub detection.

max_size.description: Maximum number of pattern results to return.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_search_ddl
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search SQL body scripts for a text pattern.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Performs a regex search across view, procedure, and function DDL bodies. Returns matching lines with context.

query.description: Regular expression to match against SQL bodies.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_get_neighbor_columns
languageModelTools.userDescription: Inspect a neighbor's columns for pruning decisions during active SM exploration.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns structural metadata (columns, types, nullability, foreign keys) for direct neighbors. Use this exclusively when the focus DDL is opaque (e.g., 'SELECT *' or ambiguous joins) and the column names are hidden. For explicit DDL, derive the structure directly from the text instead. DDL text is not returned. Pass neighbor ids only, excluding the focus node itself.

ids.description: Canonical direct-neighbor IDs whose structural columns are hidden by opaque focus DDL.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_get_screen_state
languageModelTools.userDescription: Shows what is currently on screen: active trace, analysis, or applied bookmark.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns what the user currently sees in the lineage graph: the active trace (origin, depth, nodes added or pruned by hand), the active graph analysis (type, selected group), the applied bookmark (name, source; for an AI-authored bookmark also the original run question, start object, scope and open questions), and the view level. Call this when the user says "this trace", "the analysis I ran", "this view / bookmark", or "what am I looking at". Use lineage_get_context for schemas, statistics and filters instead. Without input it returns the screen card. When an AI-authored bookmark is applied, the run that produced it is stored with the bookmark: pass ids to recall what that run found about specific objects (summary, decision with its reason, and whether the object's definition changed since), or pass filter to list one class — "pruned" (objects removed, with the reason), "open_leads" (questions the run left open), "stale" (objects whose definition changed since the run). Recalled findings describe an object as it was at run time; for a stale object, confirm with lineage_get_object_detail before answering.

ids.description: Canonical object ids, e.g. "[dbo].[factsales]", to recall from the stored run. Use without filter.

filter.description: One class of the stored run to list: pruned, open_leads, or stale. Use without ids.
